title: Test
description:
test or it defines a set of related expectations. It receives the test name and a function that holds the expectations to test.

Optionally, you can provide a timeout (in milliseconds) for specifying how long to wait before terminating, or a set of additional options. The default timeout is 5 seconds, and can be configured globally with testTimeout.

When a test function returns a promise, the runner will wait until it is resolved to collect async expectations. If the promise is rejected, the test will fail.

entries.description:
test or it defines a set of related expectations. It receives the test name and a function that holds the expectations to test.

Optionally, you can provide a timeout (in milliseconds) for specifying how long to wait before terminating, or a set of additional options. The default timeout is 5 seconds, and can be configured globally with testTimeout.

When a test function returns a promise, the runner will wait until it is resolved to collect async expectations. If the promise is rejected, the test will fail.
notes: WARNINGIf the first argument is a function, its name property will be used as the name of the test. The function itself will not be called.If test body is not provided, the test is marked as todo.

TIPIn Jest, TestFunction can also be of type (done: DoneCallback) => void. If this form is used, the test will not be concluded until done is called. You can achieve the same using an async function, see the Migration guide Done Callback section.

children.name: retry
children.description:
Retry configuration for the test. If a number, specifies how many times to retry. If an object, allows fine-grained retry control.

Note that the object configuration is available only since Vitest 4.1.
signatures:
type Retry = number | {
  /**
   * The number of times to retry the test if it fails.
   * @default 0
   */
  count?: number
  /**
   * Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts.
   * @default 0
   */
  delay?: number
  /**
   * Condition to determine if a test should be retried based on the error.
   * - If a RegExp, it is tested against the error message
   * - If a function, called with the TestError object; return true to retry
   *
   * NOTE: Functions can only be used in test files, not in vitest.config.ts,
   * because the configuration is serialized when passed to worker threads.
   *
   * @default undefined (retry on all errors)
   */
  condition?: RegExp | ((error: TestError) => boolean)
}

examples.code:

}

children.name: repeats
children.description:
How many times the test will run again. If set to 0 (the default), the test will run only one time.

This can be useful for debugging flaky tests.

children.name: tags 4.1.0+
children.description: Custom user tags. If the tag is not specified in the configuration, the test will fail before it starts, unless strictTags is disabled manually.

children.name: meta 4.1.0+
children.description: Attaches custom metadata available in reporters.

children.name: concurrent
children.description:
Whether this test run concurrently with other concurrent tests in the suite.

Set concurrent to false to opt out of concurrency inherited from describe.concurrent or sequence.concurrent:

children.name: skip
children.description: Whether the test should be skipped.

children.name: only
children.description: Should this test be the only one running in a suite.

children.name: todo
children.description: Whether the test should be skipped and marked as a todo.

children.name: fails
children.description: Whether the test is expected to fail. If it does, the test will pass, otherwise it will fail.

children.name: test.extend
children.description: Use test.extend to extend the test context with custom fixtures. This will return a new test and it's also extendable, so you can compose more fixtures or override existing ones by extending it as you need. See Extend Test Context for more information.

children.name: test.override 4.1.0+
children.description: Use test.override to override fixture values for all tests within the current suite and its nested suites. This must be called at the top level of a describe block. See Overriding Fixture Values for more information.

children.name: test.scoped 3.1.0+ deprecated
children.description: Alias of test.override
notes: DEPRECATEDtest.scoped is deprecated in favor of test.override and will be removed in a future major version.

children.name: test.skip
children.description:
If you want to skip running certain tests, but you don't want to delete the code due to any reason, you can use test.skip to avoid running them.

children.name: test.skipIf
children.description:
In some cases you might run tests multiple times with different environments, and some of the tests might be environment-specific. Instead of wrapping the test code with if, you can use test.skipIf to skip the test whenever the condition is truthy.

Unlike test.skip, test.skipIf always sets the skip option: true if the condition is truthy, false otherwise. A falsy condition overrides skip inherited from tags, the same as test(name, { skip: false }).

children.name: test.runIf
children.description: Opposite of test.skipIf. It always sets the skip option: false if the condition is truthy, true otherwise.

children.name: test.only
children.description:
Use test.only to only run certain tests in a given suite. This is useful when debugging.

Sometimes it is very useful to run only tests in a certain file, ignoring all other tests from the whole test suite, which pollute the output.

In order to do that, run vitest with specific file containing the tests in question:

examples.code: vitest interesting.test.ts

notes: WARNINGVitest detects when tests are running in CI and will throw an error if any test has only flag. You can configure this behaviour via allowOnly option.

children.name: test.concurrent
children.description:
test.concurrent marks consecutive tests to be run in parallel. It receives the test name, an async function with the tests to collect, and an optional timeout (in milliseconds).

test.skip, test.only, and test.todo works with concurrent tests. All the following combinations are valid:

When running concurrent tests, Snapshots and Assertions must use expect from the local Test Context to ensure the right test is detected.

Note that if tests are synchronous, Vitest will still run them sequentially.

examples.code:
test.concurrent(/* ... */)
test.skip.concurrent(/* ... */) // or test.concurrent.skip(/* ... */)
test.only.concurrent(/* ... */) // or test.concurrent.only(/* ... */)
test.todo.concurrent(/* ... */) // or test.concurrent.todo(/* ... */)

children.name: test.todo
children.description: Use test.todo to stub tests to be implemented later. An entry will be shown in the report for the tests so you know how many tests you still need to implement.
notes: TIPVitest will automatically mark test as todo if test has no body.

children.name: test.fails
children.description:
Use test.fails to indicate that an assertion will fail explicitly.

This flag is useful to track difference in behaviour of your library over time. For example, you can define a failing test without fixing the issue yet due to time constraints. Tests marked with fails are tracked in the test summary since Vitest 4.1.

children.name: test.each
children.description:
Use test.each when you need to run the same test with different variables. You can inject parameters with printf formatting in the test name in the order of the test function parameters.

children.name: bench experimental
notes: Updated in Vitest 5The benchmarking API has been rewritten. bench is no longer a top-level import from vitest, and the bench.skip / bench.only / bench.todo helpers have been removed. bench is now a test-context fixture accessed from inside a test().See the Benchmarking guide for the new API.
